## Core Concept
A roguelike action-strategy game built arou
nd **timeline loops**. Each run represents a different timeline.
The player alternates between **Cable** and a **Phoenix Host**.
Progress across runs unlocks new abilities, narrative layers, a

nd global system upgrades.

ike Timeline Progression

ve → Repeat

consumes stability.

ns** (High-Intensity Power Expression)

uild, renew, or reshape existence

**

istakes

s, but avoid collapse into Dark Phoenix.

ality-warping abilities

hoenix Break** → Universe resets a timeline prematurely.

e Summers (Meta-System)

# Cable & Phoenix Force Parallels Reframed for Game Development

## Core Concept
Think of the Phoenix Force and Cable as two dif
ferent **engine systems** built from the same **core codebase**,
but deployed at **different scales** and with **different runti

me constraints**.

- The **Phoenix Force** = a **Universe Engine
** that runs on infinite resources and controls creation, destru

ction, and asset resets across all worlds.
- **Cable** = a **Hig
h-Performance Player Character System** that has the same potent
ial feature set, but is running under **constant CPU drain** (th
e T-O Virus), limiting how many high-level abilities can run at

once.

Both come from the **Summers-Grey Code Tree**, meaning th
ey share the same **core engine architecture** and can theoretic

ally run the same power modules.

---

## I. Shared Codebase = S

hared Character Controller

The Summers-Grey lineage acts like a
**base CharacterController script** that supports extremely hig

h skill ceilings.

- **Jean Grey** = Primary character class des

igned to run the **Phoenix Module** without crashing.
- **Rachel
Summers** = Alternate character build capable of the same modul

e.
- **Cable** = A build **with the same character class**, but

currently running with **active debuffs**.

The architecture sup
ports **Omega-Level stats**, but whether those stats are availab

le depends on runtime load.

---

## II. The Limiter Problem = R

untime Performance Caps

### Cable’s T-O Virus
Acts like a **bac

kground thread constantly eating CPU cycles**.

- If Cable frees

up CPU (power), he unlocks **God Mode** temporarily.
- If he sl

ips, the background process **overwrites the entire system**.

#

## Phoenix Force Host Stability
The Phoenix Force needs a host w

ith:
- **High Stability** (mental resilience → memory integrity)
- **High Processing Bandwidth** (psionic throughput → GPU budge

t)

If the host can’t manage the load:
- The system enters **Dar
k Phoenix Mode** → catastrophic memory corruption → star system

wipe.

---

haracter/System | Game Development Role | Gameplay Loop |

--|---|

ets and large-scale balance patches |
| Cable | **Player Charact
er With Timeline Editing Tools** | Applies micro-patches to prev

ent bad end-states |
| Hope Summers | **Key Patch File / Expansi
on Pack** | Restores player population and gameplay ecosystem |
Cable’s mission to protect Hope = **escort mission for the futu

re patch that restores the game’s entire playerbase**.

IV. Sanctuary States = Development Environments

ame Dev Equivalent | Purpose |

oom** | **Master Build Server / Source of Truth** | Holds all Ph
